extracted.intended_audience: Researchers/authors submitting CHI 2022 Papers (HCI conference paper authors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluation/production requirements for preparing and submitting Papers to the ACM CHI 2022 conference, including formatting, anonymization, supplementary materials, review expectations, and presentation/publication obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality / prior and concurrent submission policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Your submission must be original; it cannot be published or under concurrent review elsewhere. If you make multiple submissions to CHI 2022 Papers, they must be distinct from each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have any concurrent submissions to CHI that are closely related, you must include an anonymized version of that submission as supplementary material. The same rule applies if your submission is built directly on a project described in unpublished work or currently under review at other venues. See the ACM guide on prior and simultaneous submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymization requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Your submission must be anonymized; please ensure that your submission conforms to the Anonymization Policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers that violate the anonymization policy, including within the supplemental materials, will be desk rejected. All supplementary material must be anonymized. Failure to anonymize supplemental materials will result in desk rejection of the entire submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review template and format (single-column)
rubrics_metrics.description: CHI 2022 papers are reviewed in the single column ACM template, available for both LaTeX and Word. In the LaTeX format, use \documentclass[manuscript,review,anonymous]{acmart}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A single column format must be used for the reviewing phase. Use of different templates or formats may result in desk reject. Accepted papers will be produced from LaTeX or Word source files into a single column HTML document and a two column PDF for publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission file types and anonymized source
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions are anonymized, single column PDF and source documents; a maximum 150-word abstract (based on the appropriate template).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide both PDF and source. Ensure metadata and source are prepared for review in anonymized form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract length limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstract must be a maximum of 150 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract (title, abstract, authors, subcommittee choices, and other metadata) must be submitted by the abstract deadline. The abstract is part of the submission metadata.

rubrics_metrics.name: No fixed page limit — length proportional to contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no page limit; authors are encouraged to submit a paper of length proportional to its contribution and there are no arbitrary maximum (or minimum) length papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The length of typical submissions is expected to be approximately 7,000–8,000 words excluding references and figure/table captions. Significantly longer (or shorter) submissions will be subject to additional scrutiny. Papers whose lengths are incommensurate with their contributions will be rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigor and reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers must include enough detail that the research can be reviewed for rigor and reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers that do not include enough detail to adequately assess the research may be rejected in the early reject phase. Authors are encouraged to include survey text, experimental protocols, source code, and data as supplementary material to help others replicate the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility of submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are strongly encouraged to work on improving the accessibility of their papers, including adding figure descriptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have questions about creating accessible submissions, contact the Accessibility Chairs. Advice on PDF tagging is provided (e.g., Adobe Acrobat Pro trial). If you cannot tag PDFs yourself, you may send the PDF to Accessibility Chairs after you are confident no more corrections will be made to avoid repeated retagging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary materials rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary materials (video figures, survey text, protocols, source code, data, anonymized related submissions) are optional but may be submitted to support reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Video figures: no specified time limit but recommended staying within 5 minutes; details in the Guide to Submitting a Video. Other non-video supplementary material should be submitted as a single .zip file including a README describing the materials. Reviewers are not required to review supplementary materials; the paper must stand on its own. All supplementary material must be anonymized; non-anonymized supplemental materials will result in desk rejection of the entire submission. If your submission is related to a concurrent submission or unpublished paper, you must upload an anonymized version of that paper as supplementary material. Failure to disclose related concurrent submissions may result in desk rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcommittee selection responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: When submitting, authors must select up to two appropriate subcommittees whose mandates best fit the submission topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is the authors' responsibility to select the subcommittees that offer the best expertise to assess the research. The program committee may reassign submissions to a different subcommittee if the selected ones lack adequate expertise. If unsure, email subcommittee chairs for advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revise and Resubmit phase
rubrics_metrics.description: CHI 2022 Papers will include a revise and resubmit phase to the review process, where authors can respond to reviewer feedback and improve their paper as part of the review cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This replaces the rebuttal process, giving authors time to revise and resubmit their work for CHI 2022. Submission site opens for resubmission and specific resubmission deadlines are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation requirement at conference
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must present accepted papers at the CHI Conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepted manuscripts appear in the Proceedings and in the ACM Digital Library. Papers whose authors are not at the conference to present their paper may be withdrawn from the ACM Digital Library. Details about presentation format (duration, live/pre-recorded) will be provided in the Guide to a Successful Presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core acceptance evaluation dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepted papers will excel in originality, significance, validity, reproducibility, and presentation quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CHI Papers are highly competitive and should demonstrate impact on HCI theory, method, and practice. Submissions may come from any area of HCI activity (academia/industry; science/engineering/craft; analysis/design).

rubrics_metrics.name: Desk rejection triggers and early reject risks
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain policy violations and format errors can lead to desk rejection or early rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples explicitly called out: violations of the anonymization policy (including in supplemental materials), use of incorrect templates/formats, non-anonymized supplemental materials, and failure to disclose related concurrent submissions. Papers lacking sufficient detail for rigor/reproducibility may be rejected in the early reject phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final submission metadata and publication-ready requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For final submission, source documents and metadata must be provided; all metadata in PCS must exactly match the source documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors will receive instructions for preparing and submitting a final version by the publication-ready deadline. Publication-ready versions must follow the new ACM LaTeX and Word templates. Initial upload to TAPS and publication-ready deadlines are strict; failure to meet requirements by the publication-ready deadline may lead to removal from the program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissions and rights for media/content
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtaining permissions to use video, audio, or pictures of identifiable people or proprietary content rests with the author, not ACM or CHI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are responsible for securing necessary permissions and for assigning either copyright or license to ACM or paying a fee for Open Access as required. Links to ACM rights management and authorizer service are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional promotional/preview materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors will be asked to submit a 30-second video preview summarizing the paper; this is optional but highly encouraged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preview increases the visibility of the paper before, at the conference, and in the ACM Digital Library in perpetuity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access and archival publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepted manuscripts appear in the Proceedings of the ACM Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems and are archived in the ACM Digital Library; ACM supports Gold and Green open access options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corresponding authors from ACM Open institutions will be published Gold Open Access. Authors must comply with ACM rights management procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict deadlines and no extensions policy
rubrics_metrics.description: All submission materials must be submitted before stated deadlines; no extensions will be granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important dates (abstract deadline, submission deadline, resubmission windows, publication-ready deadlines, video deadlines, etc.) are listed and all times are in Anywhere on Earth (AoE) time zone. When the deadline is day D, the last time to submit is when D ends AoE.
